result.text:
Done — all three improvements are implemented, with the 16 original tests untouched and 39 new ones added (55 passing).

## Design

**Commands as objects** (`command.py` + 5 subclasses): the `is_..._command`/if-chain in `process_command` is gone. `Command.for_character` finds the command class by iterating `__subclasses__()`, mirroring the existing `CrawlerFacing.facing`. Each command knows `execute_on` *and* `undo_on` a crawler — which is exactly what the guarded run needs. `NoCommand` is the null object for "no last command", so `"0"`, `"a00"`, `"(0)"`, `"(a)0"` are rejected with no `None` checks.

**Repetition**: a digit repeats the last command `digit + 2` more times (`"a0"` → 3 advances total). Repeating sets the last command to `NoCommand`, which makes a second digit invalid; each run has its own last command, so a digit never crosses a parenthesis.

**Sonar/grounds** (`ground.py`, `firm_sand.py`, `silt.py`, `boulder.py`, `sonar.py`, `firm_sand_sonar.py`, `ground_map_sonar.py`): no `if` asks the ground type. A ground answers `move_crawler_towards` (asked of the target position) and `assert_can_be_occupied` (asked of the current position before turning); `Boulder` signals on both, `Silt` slides, `FirmSand`/`Silt` turn normally. `Silt` slides `randrange(10) + 1` cells — I verified against real randomness that `"a"` onto silt at `(1,3)` lands exactly in `(1,3)`..`(1,12)`, the statement's range. `at_facing` still works (firm-sand sonar); `at_facing_with_sonar` is the new creation message.

**Runs** (`run.py`, `normal_run.py`, `guarded_run.py`): the crawler delegates each character to its current run. `'('`, `')'` and `finish()` are polymorphic on the run, so nesting, an unmatched `')'` and an unfinished guarded run each signal their own error. `GuardedRun.process` wraps every character, so *any* failure undoes the executed commands in reverse (raw, ground-unaware moves) and re-raises; `process` resets the run in a `finally` so a crawler survives a failed guarded run. Silt-during-guard is double dispatch: `Silt` → crawler → run, where `NormalRun` slides and `GuardedRun` signals.

## Tests worth noting (cases beyond the statement)

Partial execution of a repeated command stopped by a boulder in a *normal* run (no undo); a guarded run not undoing commands processed before it or after `)`; turning while standing on silt inside a guarded run (allowed); the slide limit actually asked of the random; reusing the crawler — including a new guarded run — after one fails; and the multi-guarded-run sequence `"aha(aagt3)aa(ht)"` → `Point(3, -1)` facing Right.

One correction to my own work: I initially wrote `"a9"` as 11 advances; it is 12 (`1 + 9 + 2`), and the test now asserts `Point(1, 14)`.

`README.md` has a new section documenting these decisions.
